### Readiness view
Historical consolidated financial work can proceed with bounded limitations. Complete financing covenant analysis cannot proceed without governing financing documents. The acquisition agreement is executed, but it does not establish the proposed loans' legal terms. Marketing financials and presentation graphics remain subject to explicit evidence limitations.

### Analytical read-through and authority hierarchy
**Historical financial foundation.** K p.1 states “For the fiscal year ended January 28, 2014”; K p.96 labels that period “Fiscal 2013.” K p.90 reports statements “in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.” This establishes a filed, audited consolidated financial anchor, not standalone borrower or restricted-group accounts. Q-A p.5 and Q-J p.5 explicitly describe their statements as “unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements”; their authority is filed interim reporting, not an annual audit.

K pp.92–95 locates balance sheets, operations, equity and cash flows. Q-A pp.3–5 locates quarter statements; Q-J pp.3–5 separates operations for “Thirteen Weeks Ended” and “Twenty-Six Weeks Ended,” while cash flows use the latter basis. This supports period-specific extraction but not treating first-half cash flows as a discrete quarter. Statement headers say “in thousands” with share/per-share exceptions; dollar-denominated reporting is retained as presented, with USD the context reporting convention. LP p.5 instead says “($ in millions),” while LP p.20 says “($ in '000).” These units must remain attached to their own evidence; no conversion was performed here.

**Comparability is documented, not resolved.** K p.96 says cash-flow reclassifications had “no effect on our previously reported net cash provided by operating activities.” Q-J p.6 states the inventory-method change “has not been retrospectively applied to prior periods.” Q-J p.7 states “Fiscal 2014” “consists of 53 weeks,” whereas the prior fiscal year “consisted of 52 weeks.” These are source-basis qualifications for downstream comparisons, not permission to normalize periods during readiness.

**Financial supplements are usable only with attribution.** K pp.50–51 and Q-A pp.30–31 locate definitions, reconciliations and footnotes; K p.50 warns “certain other costs that may recur in future periods.” Q-J p.23 locates sales progression, comparable-store performance and narrative drivers and points to its reported-to-adjusted reconciliation. LP pp.17–19 supplies preliminary acquisition/EBITDA bridges and new-store adjustments, but LP p.17 says acquired-entity measures “may not be entirely comparable” and that statements for completed acquisitions and bolt-ons “have not been audited or reviewed.” L-K p.2 says prospective measures lack a quantitative GAAP reconciliation because it is “not reasonably practicable.” Evidence risk is therefore perimeter and measurement uncertainty: downstream work can extract attributed bridges, but cannot relabel them audited reported earnings or endorse adjustments merely because a table exists.

**Entity roles are distinguishable but not fully mapped.** Q-J p.12 identifies Mattress Holding Corp. as “an indirect consolidated subsidiary”; Q-J p.14 identifies its immediate parent “Mattress Holdco, Inc.” and existing/future subsidiary guarantors subject to exceptions. A-K p.1 identifies Mattress Firm, Inc. as acquisition buyer and “wholly owned indirect subsidiary” of the public registrant. LP pp.14–15 names the proposed borrower and guarantor classes, including restricted subsidiaries and exceptions, but its organizational-structure content is graphic-degraded. Public parent, borrower, immediate holding company, acquisition buyer and target businesses must not be conflated. Exact restricted/unrestricted designations, guarantor schedules and final collateral exceptions remain unestablished.

**Acquisition documents are not financing documents.** APA p.1 says “Execution Version”; p.57 states “the Parties hereto have executed this Agreement” and includes the buyer's “/s/ Alex Weiss.” APA p.10 locates the price clause: “shall be $60,000,000, subject to certain adjustments as set forth herein.” APA pp.10–12 locates working-capital definitions and schedule dependencies, not a finalized closing statement. A-K p.2 says closing “remains subject to customary closing conditions.” PR p.1 corroborates intended cash/revolver funding but remains an announcement. The closing itself and actual funded price are not established by these sources.

APA p.57 states “schedules and exhibits have been omitted.” Its p.58 lists financial statements, facility sales, encumbrances, leases and accounting-practices schedules. The attached escrow text is headed “Form of Escrow Agreement” and begins “August [ ], 2014.” The acquisition agreement's executed status must not silently extend to its form attachment or absent schedules.

**Proposed refinancing cannot establish legal capacity.** L-K p.1 states: “The presentation contains proposed debt terms, which have not been negotiated and remain subject to change.” LP p.15 directs readers to “the Marketing Term Sheet,” which is not supplied. LP pp.14–15 provides useful proposed borrowing-base, covenant, prepayment, collateral and guarantor summaries, not operative definitions or complete baskets. LP p.20 uses “estimated 65% NOLV for illustrative purposes” and refers to an appraisal to be posted. Thus neither effective loan permissions nor actual borrowing-base availability can be certified from marketing materials.

All are retained; none is discarded as decoration or duplicate. Printed slide numbering is embedded within tool pages. Missing numerical series in chart-heavy pages and the organizational slide are parse gaps, not implied inspections of underlying visuals.

### Conflicts and version control
No irreconcilable factual conflict was established in retained evidence. Differences in date, perimeter and precision are not reconciled here. In particular, the proposed refinancing is distinct from the existing facility, and the management pro forma perimeter is distinct from the filed consolidated reporting perimeter.

A potential authority conflict is resolved only for classification: context describes legal attachments as “draft,” whereas APA p.1 says “Execution Version” and p.57 contains executed signatures. Located issuer evidence controls APA status; the context remains settings only. The proposed loans still lack executed documentation. K p.118 and Q-J p.13 describe different scheduled quarterly installment amounts; both source versions are retained for downstream debt-rollforward investigation, without declaring one an error or reconciling the change during readiness.
